name: Anterolateral (Watson-Jones) approach to the hip (periprosthetic)
corridor: Anterolateral interval between tensor fasciae latae and gluteus medius, releasing anterior vastus lateralis to reach the anterior hip capsule and femoral neck

positioning.text: Position supine or lateral with the greater trochanter and proximal femur accessible.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the lateral greater trochanter and the iliac crest tubercle.

incision.text: Start a slightly anteriorly curved incision about 7 to 10 cm proximal to the lateral greater trochanter and extend it about 10 cm distal to the trochanter.

superficial_interval.text: Incise the fascia lata and develop the interval between the gluteus medius and the tensor fasciae latae, ligating or cauterizing the vessels crossing it.

deep_interval.text: Retract the tensor fasciae latae anteriorly and gluteus medius posteriorly, release vastus lateralis from the anterior inferior trochanteric region, and open a T-shaped capsulotomy with anterior and posterior stay sutures.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, fascia lata, the tensor fasciae latae and gluteus medius interval, vastus lateralis, and the anterior hip capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The superior gluteal nerve, which crosses about 3 to 5 cm proximal to the greater trochanter, limits proximal dissection between the medius and tensor fasciae latae.

danger_zones.text: Proximal dissection more than 3 to 5 cm above the trochanter between medius and tensor fasciae latae is the danger zone for the superior gluteal nerve.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid excessive proximal retraction of the gluteus medius that endangers the superior gluteal nerve.

exposure.text: Exposes the anterior hip capsule, femoral head, and neck, though access to the joint is somewhat limited.

limitations.text: The approach gives somewhat limited access to the hip joint and less distal femoral exposure than the direct lateral approach.

indications.text: Indicated for open reduction of proximal periprosthetic femoral fractures and for revision arthroplasty.

closure.text: Repair the capsule, reattach vastus lateralis, and close the fascia lata in layers.

complications.text: Complications include superior gluteal nerve injury with abductor weakness, periarticular ossification, and hematoma.

procedure_applications.condition: A proximal periprosthetic femoral fracture is exposed through an anterolateral interval

questions.question: Which interval defines the Watson-Jones approach?
questions.answer: Between the gluteus medius and the tensor fasciae latae.

questions.question: Which nerve limits proximal dissection in this interval?
questions.answer: The superior gluteal nerve, about 3 to 5 cm above the greater trochanter.

questions.question: What is a noted limitation of the anterolateral approach?
questions.answer: Somewhat limited access to the hip joint.
